title: Claim
description: The unit of content (METHODS.md §6): a PECO-form statement tied to evidence anchors (page-located data, never reproduced passages), GRADE-rated and status-flagged.

substance.description: Substance slug from TIER1.md folder name, lowercased.

statement.description: Rendered sentence in the fixed form of METHODS §6.1.

relation.description: METHODS §6.1. 'increases', 'reduces' and 'causes' are causal and need a design and certainty that support them; 'describes' is for descriptive claims (prevalence, base rates, trends, standardized mortality), which are never upgraded for a large effect (§6.3).

magnitude.description: Direction and size with interval; absolute alongside relative where base rate known.

evidence.description: Evidence anchors (METHODS §6.2). An anchor points to where in the source the supporting data are, and states those data in the editors' own words. Passages are not reproduced.

page.description: For a PDF, the printed page(s), e.g. 'p. 379' or 'pp. 744–745' (online-first PDFs: the article's own page numbers); for a web full text without print pagination, 'PMC HTML' or 'publisher HTML'; for a trial registry, 'registry record'. '[to be located]' while unchecked (METHODS §6.2).

locator.description: Where in the source (METHODS §6.2): the section path as printed and the running-text paragraph (headings, captions, legends and footnotes are not counted), or the table or figure with its row or column, e.g. 'Results › Sample, 2nd paragraph; Table 2'.

extracted.description: The data the claim rests on, in the editors' words: numbers, n, intervals, test statistics, conditions. Never a copied passage.

quote.description: Optional verbatim wording, 15 words or fewer, only where the wording itself is the evidence (e.g. an author conclusion being appraised). At most one per claim.

anchor_status.description: unchecked: drafted, not yet located in the full text; ai-located: located in the full text by an AI reader (the first reader, or the editor from the full text or a study-card finding; located_by says which); ai-checked: confirmed by a second AI reader, re-found blind (check_mode blind) or checked at the stated place (check_mode targeted); senior-verified: checked against the source by the senior author (METHODS §5.5, §6.2).

source_read.description: What was read: 'PDF' (file in PDFs/), 'PMC full text PMCxxxxx', 'publisher full text (HTML), <journal or URL>', or 'ClinicalTrials.gov record <id>' (METHODS §5.5).

senior_note.description: The senior author's note on this anchor, from the review queue.

check_mode.description: How the second AI reader confirmed the anchor: re-found without seeing the first reader's anchors (blind), or checked at the place the first reader gave because the blind reading did not re-find it or the anchor was added later (targeted; shown as 'checked at the stated place'). card-check: the anchor was written after the second reader's card check, and its number and place match a key finding that second reader confirmed at the stated place (shown, like targeted, as 'checked at the stated place').

check_note.description: Optional: what the checker confirmed or corrected at the stated place (for targeted checks especially).

starting_level.description: high for randomized, low for observational.

status.description: METHODS §6.4. replicated: at least two independent studies in the same direction; replicated-same-team: two or more studies in the same direction from one team, site or sample, which is not independent replication.

METHODS §12. ai-anchored: every anchor located in the full text and confirmed by a second AI reader, blind or at the stated place; anchor-verified: every anchor checked by the senior author; appraised: in addition, every study card the claim rests on read against its source by the senior author.

plain.description: Plain-language sentence for readers (METHODS §9); must say no more than the statement.

senior_review.description: Senior author's decision, recorded from the review queue.

claim_version.description: The claim version the decision was made on; a decision on an earlier version does not carry over to a changed claim (METHODS §5.5).
